prompt.context: You are going to visit a client who sells golf balls in Japan. Having had no time for background research, you sit on the plane wondering about the size of the market for golf balls in Japan, and what drives demand. Your plane lands in fifteen minutes.
prompt.question: How large is the market for golf balls in Japan, and what drives demand?

clarifying_info.q: What is the population of Japan?

framework: Define the market: end-user (consumer) demand for golf balls in Japan
Segment the population: identify what share plays golf
Estimate usage: frequency of play and balls used per round
Calculate market size: population × golfer share × rounds/year × balls/round
Identify other demand drivers beyond end-user consumption

questions.prompt: Estimate the total annual market size for golf balls in Japan (number of balls)
questions.guidance: Candidate should walk through a clear linear chain of assumptions, justify each, use round numbers, and arrive at a defensible estimate. Bonus: acknowledge limitations and other demand drivers such as golf course purchases, corporate advertising/promotional balls, and range/practice balls.

math.setup: Total balls = Population × proportion who play golf × rounds per year × balls used per round
steps: Average rounds per year per golfer = 20
math.answer: 2,000 million balls, i.e. approximately 2 billion golf balls per year

brainstorming.prompt: What other drivers of golf ball demand exist beyond individual golfers buying balls for their own play?

categories.name: Golf Course & Range Demand
ideas: Driving range bucket balls (range balls purchased in bulk by facilities)

categories.name: Corporate & Promotional
ideas: Companies buying branded golf balls as client gifts or advertising merchandise

categories.name: Demographic & Behavioral Nuances
ideas: Beginner golfers lose more balls per round (higher usage rate)
Aging population in Japan with more leisure time

categories.name: Channel & Distribution
ideas: Retail vs. pro shop vs. online sales mix

recommendation: The Japanese golf ball market is estimated at approximately 2 billion balls per year, primarily driven by the ~25 million active golfers each playing roughly 20 rounds and using 4 balls per round
End-user recreational demand is the dominant driver; corporate/promotional and golf-facility demand represent meaningful but secondary segments
risks: The 1/5 golfer-participation assumption is a key driver — if golf participation is lower (Japan's golf participation has declined from peak 1990s levels), the estimate could be materially high
Ball loss rates vary significantly by skill level, which affects balls-per-round assumption
Seasonal and regional variation is not captured
next_steps: Validate golfer-participation rate with industry data or Japan Golf Association figures
Segment by ball tier (premium vs. value) to assess revenue, not just unit volume
Assess client's current market share to frame the business opportunity
